subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a public compaction fallback chain now, and should Lossless/LCM `summaryModel` fallback live in the Lossless plugin or a generic context-engine SDK seam?
rationale: The current gap is real, but the fix adds provider/auth routing behavior and crosses a core compaction plus plugin/context-engine boundary, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive product/API direction.

options.title: Approve Core Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
options.body: Add `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` for embedded compaction and keep `summaryModel` fallback behavior in the Lossless plugin or a proven SDK seam.

options.title: Design One Summary Fallback Contract
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers choose one shared API for embedded compaction, Lossless, and other context-engine summaries.

options.title: Keep Fallbacks Outside Core
options.body: Decline a new core config key and ask operators to use provider plugins, compaction providers, or external routing for summarizer fallback behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve Core Plus Plugin-Owned Lossless
recommendation.body: Add `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` for embedded compaction and keep `summaryModel` fallback behavior in the Lossless plugin or a proven SDK seam.

likelyOwner.reason: Their compaction fallback and context-engine history is the closest match for deciding the core/plugin boundary of the remaining work.
